Thanks Aditya / Sarah — hi Sarah, glad to meet you. I'm kicking off the implementation planning and want to gather a few concrete inputs so our modeling/infra recommendations are scoped correctly. If you can answer the items below (even approximate numbers), we can put together a short model shortlist, token-volume projection, and a recommended pilot configuration: 

1) Traffic profile (expected MAU and requests/day for MVP; target ramp timeline).
2) Query mix (approx % short Q/A vs long-context retrieval vs multi-turn support).
3) Typical context length when you attach retrieval docs (avg and 90th percentile).
4) SLA/latency expectations for clinician-facing vs internal ops (p95 targets).
5) Any compliance constraints (data retention windows, log export requirements, encryption/KMS).
6) Peak concurrency/RPS or rough number of concurrent users during busy hours.

If you're short on time, a quick reply with estimates is enough — we'll turn that into a proposed shortlist and a cost/latency tradeoff. Proposed next step: 30-minute technical intake on Friday to review.

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Launchpad Health — initial model shortlist & sizing (draft)

Kim / team — draft recommendations based on the limited context from Aditya and the MVP doc. Will refine after Sarah's numbers but wanted to get a baseline out today.

Design constraints / assumptions (please flag if different):
- MVP traffic assumption: 3k requests/day, ramp to 15k over 6 months.
- Query mix guess: 60% short Q/A (~40-80 tokens), 30% retrieval-augmented long context (avg 1,200 tokens), 10% multi-turn care workflows (avg 800 tokens/session, 6 turns).
- Peak concurrency estimate: 30-60 concurrent requests during morning surge.

Candidate model slate (tradeoffs: latency vs cost vs context):
1) Redwood-2.7B-Chat (quantized): good low-latency baseline for short Q/A; 512-1024 token context reasonable for most short flows. Recommended for read-heavy short answers and initial MVP.
   - Typical prompt+response tokens: 120 tokens total
   - Estimated cost: low (baseline)
   - Latency: best-in-class for sub-200ms per token on dedicated capacity

2) Llama-3-13B-Chat (8k context variant): solid middle ground for retrieval RAG workflows; supports longer context windows up to 8k tokens without aggressive chunking.
   - Typical prompt+response tokens for retrieval flows: 1,400 tokens
   - Estimated cost: medium
   - Latency: moderate; recommend batching small RAG calls and KV-cache for repeated contexts

3) Mistral-Instruct-7B (dense 16k context experiment): candidate if retrieval docs are long and you want fewer calls; higher memory but good quality on instruction-style prompts.
   - Typical prompt+response tokens: 1,400–2,000
   - Estimated cost: higher; useful for long single-shot summaries

Operational recommendations:
- Two-tier routing: route short Q/A to Redwood-2.7B, route retrieval-augmented flows to Llama-3-13B (8k). Automatic fallback to Redwood-2.7B for degraded capacity.
- Cache: implement prefix / KV caching for repeated clinician prompts (reduces token spend for frequent re-checks).
- Context strategy: chunk retrieval docs into 2k-3k windows and use a sliding-window approach for summaries.

Rough token-volume projection (MVP month):
- Total tokens/day: ~ (3k requests/day) * (avg 400 tokens/request) = ~1.2M tokens/day
- Peak-hour tokens/minute: ~ 65k tokens (assumes surges)

I've attached a draft spreadsheet with per-model token-cost estimates. Will update after Sarah confirms actual distribution.

Best,
Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[attachment: model_shortlist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@launchpad.health>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launchpad Health — onboarding & modeling projections (answers)

Hi Kimberly / Ben / team — quick answers to your questions below: 

1) Traffic / ramp: MVP internal pilot = ~500 MAU; ~3k requests/day as Ben assumed. Ramp to 5k MAU over 6 months with peak pilot days hitting ~6k requests.
2) Query mix (approx): short Q/A 60% (avg 60 tokens), retrieval-augmented doc pulls 30% (avg retrieved context 1,500 tokens; response ~200 tokens), multi-turn workflows 10% (avg 800 tokens/session, ~5 turns).
3) Context length: our clinical notes vary; most are 1–3k tokens, 90th percentile ~4.5k tokens. We typically retrieve 2–3 docs per query when relevant.
4) SLA: clinician-facing p95 target 600ms; internal ops p95 1200ms acceptable for some flows.
5) Compliance: SOC2 required; long-term logs for audit (retain 12 months). KMS for keys; no EU residency requirement for pilot.
6) Concurrency: expect 35–50 concurrent during morning surge.

Attached is a small sample CSV with tokenized document lengths and a high-level data profile. Happy to jump on the Friday intake to walk through specifics.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform
Launchpad Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-23T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launchpad Health — onboarding & modeling projections (mutual action plan)

Thanks Sarah — this is very helpful and validates several of Ben's assumptions. Summarizing recommended plan for MVP and immediate actions: 

MVP model strategy (two-tier):
- Tier A (low-latency short Q/A): Redwood-2.7B-Chat (quantized). Route ~60% short Q/A here.
- Tier B (retrieval + long context): Llama-3-13B-Chat (8k) for 30% retrieval flows. Use Mistral-7B only for specific long-summary jobs if needed.

Context & caching:
- Set active context window to 8k for Tier B; chunk docs into ~2.5k windows and store embeddings for retrieval to keep calls efficient.
- Enable KV-cache for multi-turn clinician sessions to reduce repeated computation.

Sizing & cost sketch (MVP month):
- Tokens/day estimate: ~1.2M tokens/day (matches Ben).
- Peak concurrency sizing: provision for 60 concurrent requests to meet p95=600ms on clinician flows; autoscale to additional burst capacity for peak days.

Security / compliance deliverables:
- We'll provide SOC2 evidence and an audit-log export process (12-month retention). Monica, can you start the evidence package and share the SOC2 checklist?

Next steps / timeline:
1) Friday technical intake (30 min) — confirm ingestion pipeline and retrieval strategy.
2) Ben to produce final model shortlist + exact per-token cost table by EOD Friday.
3) Monica to start compliance package and share SOC2 artifacts.
4) Draft mutual action plan & pilot SOW (I will prepare and share).

Proposed call: Friday 2027-05-28 10:00am ET (I sent a separate calendar invite).

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
